ARTICLE61 scene: a calm early-1960s working port, showing how a standardized freight container can move between ship and road without unloading its contents. One plain unmarked muted-sage steel container is the clear focal point, gently suspended level by a credible dock crane and corner lifting fittings just above an empty flatbed lorry. Supporting detail one is the flatbed lorry in accurate early-1960s shape. Supporting detail two is a modest low-deck cargo vessel at the quay behind, not a modern enormous container ship; it carries a few similar steel boxes. A soft quiet harbour and ivory sky surround the scene. Strong readable spatial relationships: the container is separate from the lorry chassis, there are no wheels attached to the suspended box, four-corner lifting is physically coherent, the quay is dry land next to the water. Paint the practical transport mechanism, not world maps, economics charts, flying containers, or any written markings. View in gentle three-quarter perspective with warm daylight, breathing space and no crowd.
